nct_ctgov.title: APOLLO: The Study of an Investigational Drug, Patisiran (ALN-TTR02), for the Treatment of Transthyretin (TTR)-Mediated Amyloidosis

indication.text: Treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults.

citations.quote: ONPATTRO is indicated for the treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults.

target_moa.text: Patisiran is a transthyretin-directed small interfering RNA (siRNA) that binds RISC and directs sequence-specific degradation of TTR mRNA in hepatocytes, reducing both wild-type and mutant TTR protein (average 78% reduction in serum TTR).

citations.quote: Patisiran is a small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA) that directs sequence-specific degradation of TTR messenger RNA (mRNA) in the liver. The result is a reduction in both wild-type and mutant TTR protein. The dose of patisiran proposed for marketing has been demonstrated to reduce TTR levels by an average of 78%.

Mechanism of actionPatisiran siRNA binds to the RNA-Induced Silencing Complex (RISC) in the cytoplasm of human hepatocytes, which results in cleavage of double-stranded siRNA to a single strand within the RISC complex. modality.text: Oligonucleotide (small interfering RNA, siRNA) formulated as a lipid complex for delivery to hepatocytes.

citations.quote: ONPATRO contains a transthyretin-directed small interfering RNA and is indicated for the treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults. (1)

ONPATTRO contains patisiran, a double-stranded small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA), formulated as a lipid complex for delivery to hepatocytes. Patisiran specifically binds to a genetically conserved sequence in the 3' untranslated region (3' UTR) of mutant and wild-type transthyretin (TTR) messenger RNA (mRNA).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and >=3% more than placebo) were upper respiratory tract infections (29% vs 21%) and infusion-related reactions (19% vs 9%). Serious AV heart block occurred in 4 patisiran patients (2.7%), including 3 complete AV block, versus none on placebo.

vote.text: The application was not referred to an advisory committee because the safety profile was acceptable, the trial design was acceptable, and the efficacy findings were clear.

citations.quote: This application was not referred for review to an advisory committee because the safety profile of patisiran is acceptable for the intended population, the clinical trial design is acceptable, and the efficacy findings were clear.

detail.text: NDA received December 11, 2017 and approved effective on the date of the approval letter, with no prior complete response cycle noted.

citations.quote: We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text.

Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated December 11, 2017, received December 11, 2017, and your amendments, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Onpattro (patisiran) lipid complex injection 2mg/mL.

requirement.text: Establish a worldwide Pregnancy Surveillance Program to collect and analyze information for a minimum of 10 years on pregnancy complications and birth outcomes in women exposed to Onpattro during pregnancy.

citations.quote: 3425-1 Establish a worldwide Pregnancy Surveillance Program to collect and analyze information for a minimum of 10 years on pregnancy complications and birth outcomes in women exposed to Onpattro (patisiran) during pregnancy. Provide a complete protocol which includes details regarding how you plan to encourage patients and providers to report pregnancy exposures (e.g., telephone contact number and/or website in prescribing information), measures to ensure complete data capture regarding pregnancy outcomes and any adverse effects in offspring, and plans for comprehensive data analysis and yearly reporting.
